text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Issue of building a fifth nuclear power plant -- banned by the previous parliament -- must not break up the government, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen warned his Social Democratic Party council.
- Justice Minister Kari Hakamies says prison sentences must not be eased.
- Jaakko Iloniemi to stay head of the Centre for Finnish Business and Policy Studies (EVA) until 1999.
- Central chamber of commerce took the "Joy" out of new corporate law by demanding a change of abbreviation for public companies to "Oyj" from the proposed "Joy."
- Financial supervision Rata proposing a ban on investment company NWI-Markkinointi and Network Investment's marketing, which it says is against public decency.
- Finance Ministry says state-owned bank Postipankki's unprofitable branches should not be supported.
- Silja's SeaWind ferry was run aground on Tuesday after it hit the bottom and started taking in water, officials say.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Forest owners say wood trade may stop as sellers hit the sidelines ahead of a new agreement and new prices, but forest industry says the situation has not affected trade in January-February.
- Local radio stations hope the start-up of national commercial radio station Suomen Uutisradio in May will boost sluggish advertising overall.
- London analysts expect Partek to sell its tractor operations, saying they are not part of its core business.
- French investment bank Paribas expects copper prices to fall sharply, dragging zinc and nickel lower, although the two latter still have an excellent price outlook.
- Government prepared to discuss with unions funds to work as buffers against economic shock in European economic and monetary union, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says.
- The road authority has built roads at too low prices but the market disturbance is not nationally significant, University of Technology study says.
- Electronics manufacturing services company Elcotec Network targets 1.5 billion markka net sales this year.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish members of European parliament appealing to the EU Comission to stop cruel animal transport.
